transcript.text: Thanks everyone for sharing. Now that we have all the findings on the table, let me summarize what needs to change in the RFC before I can sign off on privacy. First, the direct protobuf publishing proposal needs to be reconsidered in light of Maya's finding -- we need an Avro compatibility gateway and 21 days of dual publishing. Second, Jon's benchmarks show we can safely cap replay workers at 4 concurrent and reduce retention to 14 days, which actually helps with the privacy posture. Third, from my side, tokenization before events enter the bus and EU region storage are hard requirements due to the precise location data in the payloads. I still need to file my privacy review record, but the requirements themselves are clear. Riley, I'd suggest we consolidate all of these into updated RFC language before any formal sign-offs.
